**Why it was a problem:** Each frontend module's remote entry embedded its own copy of `@module-federation/runtime-core`, so the same runtime was downloaded once per app. On `@openmrs/esm-login-app`, a production remote entry was about 85 kB raw (about 26 kB gzipped), and the runtime accounted for roughly two thirds of that. Every additional module added that cost again. The changeset describes the fix as making a page download the runtime once rather than once per app (`openmrs-esm-core/.changeset/mf-runtime-shipped-once.md`, lines 8-14).

**What the app shell does now:**
- It sets `experiments.provideExternalRuntime: true` in its own Module Federation build, which publishes `runtime-core` as the `_FEDERATION_RUNTIME_CORE` global for remotes to read. The build sets `optimization: { target: 'web' }` because every app shares that runtime (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/rspack.config.js`, lines 489-502).
- At startup, `src/index.ts` calls `publishFederationRuntime()`. That function publishes the stateless `@module-federation/sdk` and `@module-federation/error-codes` helpers as globals and logs an error if the runtime global is missing (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/federation-runtime.ts`, lines 26-42; `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/index.ts`, line 7).
- The app's rspack config externalises those two helpers to the globals using `ExternalsPlugin('global', …)`, and it adds a banner guard to remote entries (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/rspack-config/src/index.ts`, lines 527-551).
- `@module-federation/runtime` and `webpack-bundler-runtime` are deliberately not shared. They cache a federation instance at module scope, so sharing them causes RUNTIME-010. They stay bundled per remote, about 14 kB (`federation-runtime.ts` lines 8-11; `rspack-config/src/index.ts` lines 528-530).

**Trade-offs in the same change:** The changeset marks this as breaking. Apps built with the new tooling require an app shell of this version or newer, and an app and its shell should use the same Module Federation minor. Webpack-built remote entries grow from about 8.7 kB to about 23 kB raw, because they previously shipped no runtime at all. The changed `runtime-core` build identifier is also now shared by every app.

**Which change and ticket:** Commit `04f538d` ("(feat) Federate most of the Module Federation runtime (#1853)") added the changeset that describes this work. That changeset is titled "(feat) O3-5873: Ship the Module Federation runtime once, from the app shell". The commit message itself does not contain the ticket key, so the key comes from the changeset. I could not find a commit whose message mentions O3-5873.

Other supporting locations: `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/federation-runtime.test.ts` covers the publish call and the `provideExternalRuntime` setting, and `openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/integration-tests/src/federation-runtime.test.ts` (line 54) checks that the runtime is read from the app shell rather than bundled.

+(feat) O3-5873: Ship the Module Federation runtime once, from the app shell
+
+Remote entries no longer embed their own copy of `@module-federation/runtime-core`; the app shell
+publishes it on a global and remotes read it from there, so a page downloads it once rather than once per
+app. Measured on `@openmrs/esm-login-app`, a production remote entry drops from ~85 kB to ~32 kB raw
+(~26 kB to ~9.7 kB gzipped); the remainder is per-build federation glue plus the ~14 kB of runtime that
+has to stay per remote.
+
+Both shared configs now build with `@module-federation/enhanced` rather than the bundlers' built-in
+Module Federation plugins, which also brings the webpack path onto the Module Federation 2.0 runtime.
+Webpack-built remote entries grow as a result — ~8.7 kB to ~23 kB raw on the same app — because they
+previously shipped a classic container with no runtime at all. Neither config emits an `mf-manifest.json`
+or federated type declarations, as before.
+
+**This is a breaking change for apps and app shells upgraded separately.** An app built with this version
+of `@openmrs/rspack-config`, `@openmrs/webpack-config` or the `openmrs` CLI requires an app shell of this
+version or newer, and refuses to start under an older one with an error in the browser console naming
+itself. Apps built with older tooling keep working in the new app shell, so a distribution can mix old
+apps with a new app shell but not the reverse. An app and its app shell should also be built against the
+same Module Federation minor; a mismatch logs a warning rather than failing the load, because minor skew
+usually works and a changed runtime helper only sometimes breaks shared-dependency de-duplication. There
+is deliberately no machine-readable compatibility field yet — the app shell's own version is the contract.
+
+One consequence worth knowing: because every remote now shares the app shell's `runtime-core`, that
+build's identifier and its `experiments.optimization` settings apply to every app's federation instance.
+The app shell therefore sets only `target: 'web'`, which is true of every app in a distribution.
